task: Add a `codemie proxy restart` subcommand and fix the post-update What's-new banner so it shows notes for the installed version, stays silent in hook invocations, and stops flip-flopping between installs.

key_reasoning.reason: Two independent surfaces bundled in one run: the proxy command group (new restart subcommand reusing daemon-manager checkStatus/stopDaemon/spawnDaemon) and the update-notice path (bin/codemie.js startup notice, the shared whatsnew utility also used by the whatsnew command, and the shared last-seen-version marker). That is 3-4 components across the CLI and utility/bin layers, and one of them is a shared utility.

Several design decisions are still open. Does restart reuse the running daemon's recorded identity (clientType, telemetryMode, port) or the start defaults? Should the notes be exact-version or the range between previous and current? How are downgrades handled? How is the marker redesigned so multiple installs on different PATHs stop flip-flopping? The flip-flop root cause is also unverified on the user's machine.

Closest pattern: connect-orchestrator ensureDaemon, which already does stop-then-spawn, so restart has a precedent. Base S. Bumped to M because the acceptance criteria list variant cases (hook or piped invocation, mismatched version, multi-install marker) and no whatsnew or bin-notice test template exists. Port stability on restart (Claude Desktop and VS Code configs pin the URL) is a moderate, non-security concern.

About 5-7 modified files (proxy/index.ts, possibly daemon-manager.ts, bin/codemie.js, utils/whatsnew.ts, commands/whatsnew.ts, CHANGELOG.md, docs/COMMANDS.md and README.md) plus 1-2 new test files. The docs edits are trivial, so this stays in the M band.
